variants.headline: Party leader blunders in election debate
variants.sub: An election debate has included a blunder by {leader}, leader of {party}.
variants.body:
The leader of {party}, {leader}, has blundered in an election debate. The misstep is established, but the words involved and their effect on voters are not supplied here. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the debate event from a fabricated quotation or a claim that the election's outcome has been decided.

Workers deserve political debate about the conditions of their lives, not merely a competition in speaking neatly. A leader's blunder can deserve attention without displacing wages, safety and services from the argument. Labour should keep the standard practical and refuse to make a performance the whole measure of representation.

The performance of {target} deserves examination without assuming an electoral effect. This paper records the blunder and leaves the words involved and the public's response outside its factual account where they are unspecified. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.
